content.thinking:
I'm going through the decision order, which runs reject, escalate, return, incomplete, approve. I'm also noting that the unknown-facts rule is in section 2.2, and that the first rule to check is a days-to-submit threshold of 61 or more leading to reject.

I'm checking the reject rules next: a claim submitted 61 or more days after its earliest expense gets rejected, and a self-approved claim does too. Then a total of $5,000 or more without the Finance Director's sign-off means escalating, using the computed total. Last, any line of $75 or more without an itemised receipt means returning the claim.

I'm moving through the remaining rules now: an alcohol line means the claim gets returned, and a gift to a government official or a business or first-class airfare line means escalating. I'm also noticing a conflict, since the pre-approved business-class airfare rule seems to clash with the escalation rule above it, and I'm still working out how to represent that permissive approval.

I'm weighing whether the evaluator needs a catch-all approve rule for claims that trip nothing, since the SOP never says "approve otherwise." I'm leaning toward translating the pre-approved business-class airfare rule as an approve rule as written, and noting that it's dominated by the escalation rule above it.

I'm settling on how to handle the SOP's permissive business-class airfare rule, which means translating it as an approve rule for lines that are business-class airfare with pre-approval. I'm leaving out any catch-all approve rule, since the SOP never states one, and I'll flag that gap as a finding. Then I'm checking the collection setup, which counts over all lines.

I'm settling the collection setup now: a claim is a list of lines, one per receipt or expense, and I'm leaving out any rule for when an empty claim is acceptable since the SOP doesn't say. I'm also building the value maps, so cabin words like "business-class" and "first class" map to business and first, the amount band "$75 or more" maps to 75_or_more, and "alcohol" maps to its category, with keys trimmed and lowercase.

I'm settling the map entries now, mapping cabin words and amount bands to their normalised values, and I'm deciding which numbered sections need their own entries, leaning toward section 1 with a note and sections 2 through 4 covered by their subsections.

I'm settling how the unknown-facts case works for the director sign-off rule: if the claim's total is $5,000 or more and the sign-off status is unknown, the outcome can't be decided yet, so it goes to incomplete rather than escalate. I'll write the escalation rule to check that director_signed is "no" and leave the unknown case to the format's own handling.

I'm checking the unknowns handling in 2.2, which says a claim with any unknown required fact can't be approved, but doesn't name the incomplete outcome, so I'll pull that from section 1. I'm also noting that section 2.1 sets the decision order and 2.2 sets the unknowns rule, and I'm getting ready to write the JSON.

unknowns.text: If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the claim cannot be approved.

lines.text: A claim is a list of lines, one per receipt or expense.

rules.text: Reject a claim submitted 61 days or more after its earliest expense.
A claim totalling $5,000 or more needs the Finance Director's sign-off. Without it, escalate.
Every line of $75 or more needs an itemised receipt. If a receipt is missing or has not been attached, return the claim.
Alcohol is not reimbursable. Return any claim with a line for alcohol.
A gift to a government official must be reviewed under the anti-bribery policy. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class and first-class airfare must be reviewed. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class airfare pre-approved in writing by the Finance Director may be approved.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes and says a claim is a list of lines; this is the source of the 'lines' list. It does not say when a claim is approved in general. The only approve rule in the SOP is 4.5, so a claim that no rule matches is left without an outcome. This gap is left for a person to resolve.
Heading only; 2.1 and 2.2 are accounted for separately.
Sets the severity order: reject, escalate, return, incomplete, approve (order / order_sop).
Sets the outcome for a rule that might apply because of an unknown fact: the claim cannot be approved, so it is incomplete (unknowns).
Heading only; 3.1 to 3.3 are accounted for separately.
Heading only; 4.1 to 4.5 are accounted for separately.

Translated as written. This conflicts with 4.4: any line that matches 4.5 also matches 4.4, and escalate outranks approve under 2.1, so this rule can never decide a claim. 'May be approved' is also permissive rather than a firm instruction.
